guard: the pi start factory, re-entered by the holder's re-establish, checks the file rather than reading an acknowledged cursor as a vanished file, and seeds the mapper from the pending frame's brackets when there is one
why: THE START FACTORY USED TO RUN ONCE. The holder now re-enters it on every re-establish, and two
assumptions it made for a single start broke on the second one (Sol, review of 2026-10-12).
P1 reads an acknowledged cursor as proof the native file vanished, without looking at the file,
so a new native session can never re-establish: every retry throws the same error at 1, 2, 4
seconds and nothing written after the outage is published. P2 seeds the mapper from the log's
acknowledged brackets rather than the pending frame's, so a tool call the frozen frame opened is
unknown to the plane that comes back: its result is dropped, and the terminal tries to open a
second run while the first is still open on the wire.

mutations.name: P1 an acknowledged cursor is read as a vanished file without checking the file
mutations.note: The first cut's guard, correct for a factory that starts once and wrong for one that is re-entered with the cursor the first turns acknowledged.

mutations.name: P2 the mapper is seeded from the acknowledged brackets, not the pending frame's
mutations.find: const brackets = wal.pending === null ? wal.brackets : wal.pending.brackets;
mutations.note: The acknowledged brackets do not know the run or the tool call the frozen frame opened; the result of that call is dropped as unknown.
